evidence: Ask is a from-scratch full-stack build, not a tweak: environment/Dockerfile:17-23 creates an empty /app containing only .gitkeep, and instruction.md:13-15 requires Node/Express/SQLite in /app, node /app/server.js on PORT, GET /api/health, one process serving UI+API, durable data at /app/app.db/DB_PATH, one-time seed load, and persistence across restarts. Scope (instruction.md:1-11 plus hireops_rules.md sections 1-9) spans session auth with four roles and 401/403/404 semantics, job/candidate creation with validation, a six-stage board with one-step moves, rejection/reopen, manual ordering, interview capacity, role-scoped permissions, optimistic version conflicts (409 naming the actor), all-or-nothing bulk moves, single-level undo with conflict rules, activity log, live updates within 15s that preserve focus/drafts/scroll, paged conversations (30 at a time with anchored scroll), per-person unread and seen state, per-user drafts surviving reload and session end, and a candidate portal with strict data redaction. Smallest-submission analysis (quality-checks.md:34): (a) static page/mock - fails gates: render judge.toml:23 requires a visible wrong-password refusal then a usable signed-in workspace ('A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'); constraints judge.toml:23 requires a UI-created job and candidate read back in an independent browser context as Observer ('A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app does not satisfy the gate'). score.py:41,48 zeroes reward unless every gate > 0. (b) Single CRUD screen with auth (jobs + candidates, the gate-passing stub): functional weights total 58.5 over 43 criteria; such an app can earn at most hro_job_open 0.5 + hro_add_candidate 0.5 + hro_add_email_rules 1 = 2.0/58.5 = 0.0342. hro_anonymous, hro_observer_readonly and hro_candidate_no_staff each need replays of observed move/note/message requests with signed-in successes as controls, which a CRUD stub cannot produce, and hro_restart needs notes/messages/activity. scoring.toml:10-11 sets functional floor 0.05 and score.py:47-48 requires functional > floor, so reward = 0.0 even with perfect visual Likert scores. Polish (5 binary criteria) all require live updates, paged threads, failed-send handling or session resume, so a stub gets 0 there. Clearing the floor requires genuinely implementing board mechanics (e.g. one-stage moves 1.5 + reorder 1.5), i.e. real build work. Conforming-alternative check: the brief leaves routes, layout, labels, transport (polling/SSE/sockets) and file layout open (instruction.md:11,13; hireops_rules.md:3-5,123; app_context.md:33-34), so a valid alternative architecture is not penalised on this row's axis. Template instruction.md is a CHANGE_ME placeholder, so the task-specific prompt fully replaces it as intended; test.sh and score.py are byte-identical to the template. Reference solution is ~1600 lines across server, DB, bootstrap and three client modules, consistent with substantive build scope.
notes: Floor arithmetic is static analysis of the frozen scoring policy and criteria, not a measured weak-app run. raw-evidence-index.json states reward discrimination/ranking and configured judge runs are absent; that gap belongs to the runtime/discrimination rows and is not waived here, but it does not create a defect in this row, which judges whether the ask itself requires real build work. Margin observation (not a defect): a stub adding only 1.5 weight of real board behaviour would cross the 0.05 floor, which already requires server-side stage logic.
